$comment: Band gaps that exist in the SOURCE REGULATION, not in our encoding.
`pnpm rules:validate` fails on any band gap not listed here, so an
accidental encoding hole can never ship quietly. Adding an entry is a
claim about the printed table and needs the same scrutiny as a rule:
quote the two rows and say why the gap is real.
At runtime these surface as the `source_band_gap` flag, which names both
neighbouring rows and declines to compute (spec §9).

gaps.reason: UBBL 2016 setback table (compendium p.154): row 1 reads 'Below 100', row 2 reads 'Above 100 and up to 250'. A plot of exactly 100 m² is in neither row. The gap is in the bye-law as printed.
gaps.resolution: Open — see docs/tasks.md. Needs the verifying architect to decide whether DDA practice reads row 1 or row 2 as governing 100 m² exactly, with a citable basis. Until then the engine declines.
